He marks all my paths.'” (web:Job.33.11, oshb:Job.33.11). 2ms address to Job resumes at the next row's opening, הֶן זֹ֣את לֹא צָדַ֣קְתָּ אֶעֱנֶ֑ךָּ כִּֽי יִרְבֶּ֥ה אֱ֝ל֗וֹהַ מֵאֱנֽוֹשׁ – “"Behold, I will answer you. prev_row.boundary_rationale: Elihu turns to address Job by name: 33:1 opens the vocative naming of Job and shifts the addressee from the friends (plural, addressed across the preceding rows of this speech) to Job (singular), וְֽאוּלָ֗ם שְׁמַֽע נָ֣א אִיּ֣וֹב מִלָּ֑י וְֽכָל דְּבָרַ֥י הַאֲזִֽינָה – “"However, Job, please hear my speech, and listen to all my words.” (web:Job.33.1, oshb:Job.33.1), opening an invitation to a fair hearing that runs through the row: he has opened his mouth in sincerity (web:Job.33.2-33.3), claims the same creaturely origin as Job's Maker, הֵן אֲנִ֣י כְפִ֣יךָ לָאֵ֑ל מֵ֝חֹ֗מֶר קֹרַ֥צְתִּי גַם אָֽנִי – “Behold, I am toward God even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.” (web:Job.33.6, oshb:Job.33.6). Its companion claim, the divine-spirit clause at 33:4, רֽוּחַ אֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֑תְנִי וְנִשְׁמַ֖ת שַׁדַּ֣י תְּחַיֵּֽנִי – “The Spirit of God has made me, and the breath of the Almighty gives me life.” (web:Job.33.4, oshb:Job.33.4), is pointed byte-identical in its core to 32:8's parallel clause (pointed byte sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 32:8 and 33:4) — a byte-twinned formula binding Elihu's opening pivot to this address movement. Elihu issues a challenge, אִם תּוּכַ֥ל הֲשִׁיבֵ֑נִי עֶרְכָ֥ה לְ֝פָנַ֗י הִתְיַצָּֽבָה – “If you can, answer me. Set your words in order before me, and stand up.” (web:Job.33.5, oshb:Job.33.5), and reassures him of no terror (web:Job.33.7). The row closes before the discourse-quotation frame opens at 33:8.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this row and the quoted material after it as one longer unit was considered and rejected, since the quotation frame at 33:8 marks a change of voice from Elihu's own address to a report of Job's words.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Elihu's appeal for Job's close attention to speaking

next_row.boundary_rationale: A presentative opens a summary of the three illustrations, הֶן כָּל אֵ֭לֶּה יִפְעַל אֵ֑ל פַּעֲמַ֖יִם שָׁל֣וֹשׁ עִם גָּֽבֶר – “"Behold, God does all these things, twice, yes three times, with a man,” (web:Job.33.29, oshb:Job.33.29), echoing the thesis stated at 33:14, “For God speaks once, yes twice, though man pays no attention.” (web:Job.33.14, oshb:Job.33.14), with 33:29's own escalation to "twice, yes three times," and extending the "pit"/light language of the illustrations into a closing statement (web:Job.33.30). Elihu then addresses Job by name a second time in this speech, הַקְשֵׁ֖ב אִיּ֥וֹב שְֽׁמַֽע לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וְאָנֹכִ֥י אֲדַבֵּֽר – “Mark well, Job, and listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will speak.” (web:Job.33.31, oshb:Job.33.31), inviting a response (web:Job.33.32) before the speech closes, אִם אַ֭יִן אַתָּ֥ה שְֽׁמַֽע לִ֑י הַ֝חֲרֵ֗שׁ וַאֲאַלֶּפְךָ֥ חָכְמָֽה – “If not, listen to me. Hold your peace, and I will teach you wisdom."” (web:Job.33.33, oshb:Job.33.33). A setumah follows oshb:Job.33.33 (setumah, single-witness). The next speech opens at 34:1 with a fresh vaya'an formula, וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר — the tier-1 driver for the 33:33|34:1 seam: the formula and the mark both close this speech before the next one begins.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A referent shift from named classes of rulers to universal humanity opens this movement at oshb:Job.34.21 “כִּי עֵ֭ינָיו עַל דַּרְכֵי אִ֑ישׁ וְֽכָל צְעָדָ֥יו יִרְאֶֽה”, web:Job.34.21 “"For his eyes are on the ways of a man. He sees all his goings.” — the verse-initial causal particle כִּי is not itself a seam-grade signal here (it opens 8 of 37 verses in ch.34 alone — 34:3, 34:5, 34:9, 34:11, 34:21, 34:23, 34:31, 34:37 — and 82 book-wide, skeleton-swept over consonantal_index.json), so the row rests its near edge on the shift in referent specificity (kings/princes/nobles/rich at 34:18-20 narrowing no further, then “a man” universally at 34:21) rather than on the particle. Universal moral oversight follows: no darkness hides evildoers (34:22), no formal summons is needed before God (34:23), the mighty are broken and replaced (34:24-26), because they turned from following him (34:27), so that the cry of the poor and afflicted reaches him and he hears it (34:28), and he alone grants or withholds quietness over nation and individual alike (34:29-30). The ten verses run as one continuous argument with no address shift or discourse-frame break until the fresh quotation frame at 34:31, which is why the span sits at the upper edge of the strophe guide rather than splitting at, say, the night language of 34:25.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting this unit at the night language of 34:25 was rejected because no vocative or discourse-frame marker interrupts the argument between 34:21's opening claim and 34:30's close; the whole section elaborates one continuous claim about God's unhidden oversight.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Divine oversight spanning rulers to universal human conduct

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A conditional address opens this strophe, oshb:Job.34.16 “וְאִם בִּ֥ינָה שִׁמְעָה זֹּ֑את הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינָה לְק֣וֹל מִלָּֽי”, web:Job.34.16 “"If now you have understanding, hear this. Listen to the voice of my words.”, distinct from the plain-imperative address at 34:10, and the content turns to a fresh topic-turn interrogative at oshb:Job.34.17 “הַאַ֬ף שׂוֹנֵ֣א מִשְׁפָּ֣ט יַחֲב֑וֹשׁ וְאִם צַדִּ֖יק כַּבִּ֣יר תַּרְשִֽׁיעַ”, web:Job.34.17 “Should even one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn him who is righteous and mighty,”. The strophe develops the claim that God shows no partiality to kings, nobles, princes, or the rich (34:18-19), closing with the sudden, handless death of the mighty (34:20).
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 34:16 as a continuation of the v.10 axiom was rejected because ואם marks a new conditional address and the content turns to a fresh interrogative about impartial judgment of rulers rather than the general principle stated before it.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: God indicts kings and nobles by sovereign divine scrutiny

next_row.boundary_rationale: A hypothetical quotation frame opens this short strophe, oshb:Job.34.31 “כִּֽי אֶל אֵ֭ל הֶאָמַ֥ר נָשָׂ֗אתִי לֹ֣א אֶחְבֹּֽל”, web:Job.34.31 “"For has any said to God, 'I am guilty, but I will not offend any more.”, imagining words of repentance Job has not in fact spoken, and closing with a direct challenge to the audience: web:Job.34.33 “Shall his recompense be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore speak what you know.”. shipped_row.boundary_rationale: Elihu's third speech opens with a second vaya'an formula, oshb:Job.35.1 “וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּ וַיֹּאמַֽר”, whose skeleton is the defective אליהו (five consonants, byte-verified from consonantal_index.json) rather than the full אליהוא (six consonants) at 34:1 — the same formula family, a distinct spelling member; among the book's four Elihu formula-verses (32:6, 34:1, 35:1, 36:1) this defective spelling is attested at 1 of these 4 verses (35:1). The formula opens a fresh address, immediately putting direct second-person questions to Job that restate his claim, web:Job.35.2 “Do you think this to be your right, or do you say, ‘My righteousness is more than God’s,’”, and promising an answer: web:Job.35.4 “I will answer you, and your companions with you.”. This follows the SAMEKH-marked close of the second speech at oshb:Job.34.37 (samekh, single-witness); unlike that speech's exordium, which addressed 'the wise' about Job in the third person, this exordium addresses Job himself directly.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading 35:1 as a bare resumption of speech 2's argument was rejected because the verse-initial vaya'an formula recurs here as it did at 34:1, marking a fresh speech-opening even though the spelling of Elihu's name differs.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Third speech exordium: direct address promise to answer Job

prev_row.boundary_rationale: אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב recurs at the skeleton/consonantal tier, oshb:Job.34.34 “אַנְשֵׁ֣י לֵ֭בָב יֹ֣אמְרוּ לִ֑י וְגֶ֥בֶר חָ֝כָ֗ם שֹׁמֵ֥עַֽ לִֽי”, web:Job.34.34 “Men of understanding will tell me, yes, every wise man who hears me:” (sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 34:10 and 34:34; the niqqud differs — hataf-patah at 34:10 against sheva at 34:34), echoing the exordium's address at 34:10 as its grammatical SUBJECT here (3mp yiqtol יֹ֣אמְרוּ) rather than repeating that verse's 2mp-imperative vocative — a bracket with subject/addressee inversion opening the speech's closing strophe as the counterpart to that earlier appeal. Naming Job directly recurs here too: bare אִ֭יּוֹב at 34:35 (the SECOND bare token in this chapter, after 34:5) and אִיּ֣וֹב at 34:36 (the THIRD), a distinct count object from the prefixed כְּאִיּ֑וֹב at 34:7 that stands between them, quoting the verdict “Job speaks without knowledge” (web:Job.34.35 “'Job speaks without knowledge. His words are without wisdom.'”) and wishing him tried to the end (web:Job.34.36 “I wish that Job were tried to the end, because of his answering like wicked men.”), closing with the charge that he adds rebellion to sin, web:Job.34.37 “For he adds rebellion to his sin. He claps his hands among us, and multiplies his words against God."”. A SAMEKH mark follows oshb:Job.34.37 (samekh, single-witness) in the WLC, corroborating (not driving) the speech's end at this point.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 34:34 as a continuation of the repentance challenge above was rejected because אנשי לבב echoes the exordium's address at 34:10, marking a deliberate return to the appeal-to-the-wise register that closes the speech.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Closing verdict renaming Job, inclusio bracket on wise men

next_row.boundary_rationale: An imperative pair opens a fresh strophe, oshb:Job.35.5 “הַבֵּ֣ט שָׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וְשׁ֥וּר שְׁ֝חָקִ֗ים גָּבְה֥וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ”, web:Job.35.5 “Look to the skies, and see. See the skies, which are higher than you.”, pivoting from the promise to answer at 35:4 to a cosmic-transcendence argument developed through paired conditionals (35:6-8): sin or righteousness reaches one's fellow human beings, not God himself. The אם-clauses here are texture inside one strophe, not the extended protasis-apodosis series that structures the oath list of chapter 31.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 35:5-8 into the exordium above was rejected because the imperative pair 'look... and see' opens a distinct cosmic-transcendence argument rather than continuing the direct promise-to-answer of 35:4.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Imperative cosmic-height argument: human conduct reaches humans only

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The 2ms verb תֹ֭אמַר reopens direct second-person address to Job, oshb:Job.35.14 “אַ֣ף כִּֽי תֹ֭אמַר לֹ֣א תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ דִּ֥ין לְ֝פָנָ֗יו וּתְח֥וֹלֵֽל לֽוֹ”, web:Job.35.14 “How much less when you say you don't see him. The cause is before him, and you wait for him!”. The preceding אַ֣ף כִּֽי (skeleton sweep: 4 book-wide — 9:14, 15:16, 25:6, 35:14) is a dependent a-fortiori continuation of the clause before it in all four attested instances, not itself an independent opener; here it intensifies 35:13's אַךְ שָׁ֭וְא לֹא יִשְׁמַ֥ע אֵ֑ל וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה, and the same root crosses the row's own near seam (יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה at 35:13 against תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ at 35:14) as continuity texture disclosed here and argued against: the seam is carried instead by the shift back to direct 2ms address in תֹ֭אמַר, applying the transcendence argument specifically to Job's complaint that God does not see him. The speech, and this part, close at 35:16 with the prefixed token וְ֭אִיּוֹב, oshb:Job.35.16 “וְ֭אִיּוֹב הֶ֣בֶל יִפְצֶה פִּ֑יהוּ בִּבְלִי דַ֝֗עַת מִלִּ֥ין יַכְבִּֽר”, web:Job.35.16 “therefore Job opens his mouth with empty talk, and he multiplies words without knowledge."”. A PE mark follows oshb:Job.35.16 (petuchah, single-witness) in the WLC; the next verse, 36:1, reopens with the vayosef formula, “Elihu also continued, and said,” (web:Job.36.1), rather than the vaya'an formula that opened both 34:1 and 35:1 inside this part — a formula-family change, disclosed here as the argument for this part's far edge.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this strophe through 36:1 was rejected because 35:16 completes the verdict clause begun by the prefixed ואיוב token, and both the mark evidence (PE, single-witness) and the formula evidence (vayosef replacing vaya'an) fall on the far side of that boundary.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Verdict closing third speech: Job speaks empty without knowledge

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A new topic opens with a participant shift from the second-person argument above to a third-person scenario, oshb:Job.35.9 “מֵ֭רֹב עֲשׁוּקִ֣ים יַזְעִ֑יקוּ יְשַׁוְּע֖וּ מִזְּר֣וֹעַ רַבִּֽים”, web:Job.35.9 “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for help by reason of the arm of the mighty.”: the oppressed cry out and go unanswered (35:9-10), despite being taught by the very order of creation (35:11), because of the pride of evil men (35:12), so that God will not hear an empty cry (35:13). The shift from 'you' (Job) to 'they' (the oppressed) marks the strophe's opening edge; the return to direct address at 35:14 marks its close.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 35:9-13 as a continuation of the transcendence argument's second-person address was rejected because these verses shift to third-person description of the oppressed before the direct application back to Job resumes at 35:14.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Third-person narrative of the oppressed cry unanswered

next_row.boundary_rationale: Elihu's fourth and final movement opens on the verse-initial formula וַיֹּ֥סֶף אֱלִיה֗וּא וַיֹּאמַֽר (“Elihu also continued, and said,”, web:Job.36.1), built on the root vayosef (ויסף), NOT the vaya'an (ויען) that opens Elihu's earlier three speeches at 32:6, 34:1, and 35:1 -- the formula family itself changes here, marking Elihu RESUMING rather than a fresh interlocutor response, the same continuation-verb Job uses at 27:1 and 29:1. Verses 2-4 are Elihu's captatio: “Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to say on God’s behalf.” (web:Job.36.2), asking for patience before claiming his knowledge comes from afar, and closing on direct second-person address, תְּמִ֖ים דֵּע֣וֹת עִמָּֽךְ (‘perfect in knowledge is with you’, web:Job.36.4) -- the 2ms suffix on עמך (‘with you’) singles out Job as addressee before the doctrinal material begins at verse 5. The strophe is bounded at its close by the next presentative הן-opening at 36:5.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding 36:1 into the prior speech as a mere continuation verse was rejected because the vayosef formula still marks a fresh verse-initial discourse opening, the pattern this book treats as a seam everywhere else it occurs (27:1, 29:1).
next_row.literature_type_guess: Fourth speech captatio: Elihu resumes with patience request
